candidates.title: House members introduce bill to ban use of remote-control locomotives outside of yards
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Two members of Congress from New York state have introduced legislation that would ban the use of remote-controlled locomotives outside of railroad yards. H.R. 9409 is sponsored by U.S. Reps. Tim Kennedy, a Democrat representing the Buffalo area, and Mike Lawler, an outgoing Republican from a suburban area north of New York City. It calls for heavy penalties for violations: daily penalties of $1 million or 1% of a company’s annual income, whichever is greater. Kennedy said in a press release that those who live near railroad tracks “should have the comfort of knowing that a highly trained engineer is in the cab with their eyes directly on the track. We know that chemicals and other dangerous materials are transported on these lines; their safe handling requires experienced engineers who can react to any risks they may encounter.” Kennedy’s release notes a July 2024 incident in Niagara Falls, N.Y., in which a remote-controlled locomotive overran the end of a wye, derailed,

candidates.excerpt: CHICAGO — A public service announcement produced by the Belt Railway of Chicago is running this month to raise awareness about the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline that is available for anyone contemplating taking their life along railroad tracks. The 30- and 60-second commercials build upon an informational campaign initiated by commuter operator Metra, which has featured a locomotive wrapped with 988 messaging and installed 988 signage at all of its stations. The 988 Lifeline offers free and confidential 24-hour-a-day, seven-day-a-week counselor support by phone, text, or online chat. The 60-second spot and 30-second version can both be viewed on YouTube. Joe Chacon, the Belt Railway’s digital media coordinator who formerly led Operation Lifesaver Illinois’ board of directors, said the Federal Railroad Administration provided feedback in the development of the PSA. candidates.title: Maersk confirms order for twelve 24,000 TEU containerships
candidates.excerpt: Maersk has confirmed an order for twelve 24,000 TEU containerships, with deliveries expected in 2030 and 2031. The vessels would be the largest in the carrier’s fleet when they enter service. Maersk has not disclosed which shipyard will build the vessels. Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding, Hengli Heavy Industry and Yangzijiang Shipbuilding were previously reported to be among the contenders. The order follows an earlier contract for a series of 18,600 TEU containerships.

candidates.title: Emirates Shipping Line to launch EFIX through slot agreement
candidates.excerpt: Emirates Shipping Line will begin offering its EFIX service in mid-December through a slot agreement on an existing Far East–Indian Subcontinent loop, according to DynaLiners. The loop, marketed by its operators as CIX4, IWI, CSE and RWA2, is jointly operated by Evergreen, Interasia Lines, Pacific International Lines (PIL) and Regional Container Lines (RCL). It connects Shanghai, Ningbo and Shekou with Nhava Sheva, Mundra and Karachi via Singapore and Port Klang. DynaLiners reports that EFIX is expected to replace Emirates Shipping Line’s current CIX2 slot arrangement on a service operated by DP World Shipping Solutions, Evergreen, Ocean Network Express (ONE) and T.S. Lines. The EFIX rotation is: Shanghai – Ningbo – Shenzhen (Shekou) – Singapore – Port Klang – Nhava Sheva – Mundra – Karachi – Port Klang – Singapore – Shanghai.

candidates.title: Okee Maritime buys two newbuilds as Costamare expands capacity on five ships
candidates.excerpt: German shipowner Okee Maritime has bought two 1,800 TEU containerships under construction at Huanghai Shipbuilding, according to TradeWinds. The vessels were originally ordered by Greece’s Cosmoship and are due for delivery in mid-2027. Separately, Greek shipowner Costamare has increased the capacity of five containerships built in 2016 from 14,400 TEU to at least 15,000 TEU each. Huarun Dadong Shipyard raised the height of 17 lashing bridges to increase container capacity and carried out other modifications unrelated to the capacity upgrade.

candidates.title: Are North-South container alliances on the way?
candidates.excerpt: Are North-South container alliances on the way? Vessel-sharing agreements (VSAs) are not new to North-South routes, but the more structured and longer-lasting alliance partnerships have until now been confined to the Asia-Europe, Transpacific and Transatlantic trades, expanding only recently to the Middle East in a few isolated cases. These East-West routes handle the largest and most concentrated cargo volumes, providing the critical mass needed to justify deploying increasingly large vessels. Sharing ships enables carriers to spread operating costs, improve vessel utilisation and offer more comprehensive weekly networks without each having to operate an entirely independent service. The economics differ on North-South routes. Trades connecting Asia, Europe and North America with Latin America, Africa and Oceania generally have smaller and more fragmented cargo flows. candidates.title: Stalled exits drive growth in GP and LP financing
candidates.excerpt: Stalled exits drive growth in GP and LP financing Lending to general partners (GPs) and limited partners (LPs) is growing significantly, driven by a need for liquidity and an appetite to invest. Fokke Lucas, a partner at 17Capital, said GP and LP financing is currently one of the biggest growth areas in fund finance. “That’s where we are seeing increased volume,” he said. “We expect to continue to invest significantly in that space. We believe we are well positioned for the opportunity as we have one of the largest dedicated teams and pools of capital for this opportunity.” The main driver is the slowdown in exits, he said. Called Working Capital Finance, the facility offers between £50,000 and £500,000 over terms of up to 12 months, with rates from 1.25 per cent a month plus an arrangement fee. Momenta said the facility is designed to help SMEs buy stock and cover day-to-day running costs. The launch comes as cash flow remains one of the biggest challenges facing UK SMEs, with late payments continuing to tie up cash and hold back growth. In May, the government introduced the Small Business Protections Bill to tackle the problem. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Backlog Value Up 28% Year over Year Aftermarket Revenue Growth of 65% Year over Year Reaffirms Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook Provided on October 19 CHICAGO, November 9, 2026 – FreightCar America, Inc. (NASDAQ: RAIL) (“FreightCar America” or the “Company”), a diversified manufacturer and supplier of railroad freight cars, railcar parts and components, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter results were consistent with the preliminary results the Company announced on October 19, 2026.
